questions.qtext: Which of the following is NOT a 7 deadly disease of management defined by Deming?

options.text: Running a company on visible figures alone

questions.solution:
(a)
7 Deadly diseases of management defined by Deming are :
1. Lack of constancy of purpose.
2. Emphasis on short-term profits.
3. Evaluation by performance, merit rating, or annual review of performance.
4. Mobility of management.
5. Running a company on visible figures alone.
6. Excessive medical costs.
7. Excessive costs of warranty, caused by lawyers who work for contigency fees.

Consider the following statements regarding the risk involved in the project :
1. If the possibilities of possible outcomes of a given problem are not known, then it can be concluded that an element of risk is involved.
2. Positive risk offer benefit to the project.
3. Delphi techniques is one of the Risk information gathering technique.
Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
questions.solution:
(b)
If the possibilities of possible outcomes of a given problem are not known then it can be concluded
that an element of uncertainity is involved.
If the possibilities of outcomes is known then it can be concluded than an element of risk is involved.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements in context of reliability :
1. The reliability of system is always less than or equal to the reliability of individual component.
2. One way to increase the product reliability is to build redundancy in the form of back up plan.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(b)
The reliability of system is always less than or equal to the reliability of individual component
when they are connected in series but if the individual components are connected in parallel then
reliability of system can be greater than or equal to the reliability of individual component.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement is NOT correct with respect to the difference between histogram and bar graph?

options.text: Histogram refers to a graphical representation that displays data by way of bars to show the frequency whereas bar graph is a pictorial representation of data that uses bars to compare different categories of data.
In histogram, there are no spaces between bars whereas in bar graph are spaces between bars.
Histogram indicates distribution of non-discrete variables whereas bar graph indicates comparison of discrete variables.
Histogram represents categorical data whereas bar graph represents quantitative data.

questions.solution:
(d)
Histogram represents quantitative data whereas bar graph represents categorical data.

questions.qtext: In context of six sigma project methodology, DMADV is used in place of DMAIC:

options.text: To make improvements by eliminating defects
To fulfill the demands of customers with regard to quality that can’t be satisfied by existing process

questions.solution:
(d)
Sometimes, the demands of the customers with respect to quality cannot be satisfied by the existing
process. At times, an organization must decide to launch a new product or service to grab a new
business opportunity offered by the environment. In all such situations, the last two steps used in
the DMAIC, namely “improve” and “control” can be replaced by “design” and “verify” so that it
becomes DMADV.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement is NOT correct regarding operating characteristic (OC) curve?

options.text: To obtain ideal OC curve, the sample size should be infinite.
As the sample size increases, the OC curve becomes more and more discriminating.
The OC curve is the primary tool for representing and investing the properties of a lot acceptance sampling plan.
As the acceptance number increases keeping the lot size constant, the OC curve becomes more and more steeper.

questions.solution:
(d)
• As the sample size increases, the OC curve shape will become more steeper means tends to the
ideal OC curve and it become more discriminating between good and bad lots.
• Increasing the acceptance number does not significantly change the shape of OC curve.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements with respect to service quality :
1. Service quality is a measure of how well a delivered service matches customers’ expectations.
2. Objective service quality is the customers perceived conformity of working result with expected benefit.
3. Subjective service quality is the concrete measurable conformity of working result with previously defined benefit.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(a)
• Objective service quality is the concrete measurable conformity of a working result with
previously defined benefit.
• Subjective service quality is the customers perceived conformity of working result with expected
benefit.
